findings.title: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) did not ensure that all noted easement violations were resolved in a timely manner.
findings.description: MALPF failed to periodically review its database of easement violations to ensure follow-up and corrective actions were taken by landowners. As of January 31, 2013, the database indicated approximately 281 unresolved violations, some remaining for up to 6 years, though management considered only 31 high or medium priority. Consequently, MALPF lacked assurance that noted violations were resolved timely and that landowners complied with easement terms.

dollar_amounts.context: civil penalties per day per violation

findings.recommendation: MALPF should perform appropriate and timely follow-up actions on outstanding easement violations to ensure that corrective actions were taken; determine the current status of unresolved violations and impose penalties if deemed appropriate.

extraction.agency_response_summary: MALPF concurs with the finding and acknowledges the need for better communication among staff regarding follow-up and resolution of easement violations. They plan to have the monitoring coordinator review the database three times a year and commit to entering identified violations into the database. Staff work closely with an Assistant Attorney General to notify landowners and negotiate resolutions.
